review_kind: Independent read-only SoC/ICB/driver source review; no simulation performed by this reviewer
verdict_scope: Source-level design supports public-E203 full-W RevD_opt integration. Current full RTL/CPU execution is RUNNING; this review does not approve execution results, final submission, official platform, or physical PPA.

checks.observation: Driver reads out_y_index and task ID from a held result, rejects out-of-range/duplicate index, writes destination[index] and flag_destination[index], validates last exactly at index M*N-1, then fences and POPs. Adapter cannot advance result except explicit legal POP.

One ICB response slot and one captured event slot. icb_cmd_ready depends only on response ownership, never on a W/core slot. Full/fault COMMIT returns immediate bus error. Driver drains available result before checking capacity, and has one producer, so polling capacity then staging/commit cannot lose capacity to another producer in this model.

MMIO done is explicitly core completion sticky, not system completion. CPU writes Y and flags before POP and uses fence; the testbench counts actual shared write responses. Per-task phase completion requires all indexed writes/flags, a completed response window and accelerator done. Final system_done is a testbench observation asserted only on final CPU mailbox write response, with all output/flag response counts and final shared SRAM checked. It is not an exposed synthesizable SoC hardware status port.

Runner takes frozen vector case0 layer1 and case1 layer2, distinct W and bias hashes. Each has separate input/output region within 512KiB, unique task ID, per-run load, poisoned destinations and reset driver seen bitmap. Phase write precedes task descriptor/input loading, final window ends at last actual Y/flag response. This demonstrates two cold engineering tasks if execution passes, not twelve tasks or official600.

TB tracks every Y/flag index separately and checks real CPU command data, write masks, no duplicate/missing indices, matched response counts, starts/pops, instruction activity and final shared image. Expected arrays are TB-only; CPU-visible shared fixture contains raw X/W/b and poisoned destinations. Python post-check independently parses actual output tuples.

Adapter tests exercise last-result hold, queued BEGIN/full COMMIT and reset. Completion TB separates MMIO capture/core acceptance/retirement; queued-invalid after final ingress barrier belongs after old task completion, fault takes precedence over sticky old done. Separate bus TB tests response stability/backpressure/reset, unknown/misaligned/partial accesses. Actual compiled mutation and CPU omission scripts exist, but source presence is not test execution.

nonblocking_limitations.observation: The adapter instantiates core_stream_frontend_opt full-W. Driver preloads all W tiles and only then emits START. This is legal for full-W and must not be advertised as D4 tiled CPU integration. A future tiled adapter/driver must preload tile0, START, then feed subsequent OPEN/load/COMMIT while draining results; otherwise a future OPEN may head-of-line block START.
nonblocking_limitations.action: Keep current full-W CPU claim narrow; require independent tiled-SoC scope/tests before switching.

nonblocking_limitations.observation: Driver assumes trusted descriptor offsets/alignment and signed48 bias payload. It does not validate all byte ranges against512KiB or prevent overlap; current runner constructs valid nonoverlapping descriptors and binds source arrays.
nonblocking_limitations.action: For this bounded trusted-fixture trial this is not a blocker. For a reusable external submission API, add argument-range/alignment/overlap/error tests or document trusted descriptor preconditions.

nonblocking_limitations.observation: Public E203 shell and behavior shared RAM are reused. Simulator timescale and functional pass cannot establish official platform equivalence, macro mapping,150MHz,2.25mm2,energy score.
nonblocking_limitations.action: Keep official/physical fields NOT_RUN until actual supplied-platform/library evidence exists.

acceptance_conditions: Wait for current CPU full --tasks2 actual simulator/runner exit0 and explicit source_unchanged true; inspect actual output tuples and final CPU write responses, not a stale PASS label.

Compare bound source hashes in full and independent repeat to the final candidate hashes below (and current core_opt identity owned by core reviewer); if any bound source changes, rerun affected checks.
Run same frozen full-W driver/adapter/testbench with accepted D2 alias for matched cold CPU comparison, and report both CPU and core/frontend cycle changes separately.

Require fresh small cross-simulator/latency checks plus adapter bus/completion and real RTL mutation controls; CPU zero-return/skip-last must fail intended coverage without expected values in firmware.
Retain D2 fallback and failed/stale evidence; this provisional source review cannot independently close the final root acceptance gate.
